question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic Android execution in core, and under which command-policy and permission boundary?
rationale: The requested remaining tools can read or control sensitive phone state and may execute arbitrary code, so automation cannot choose the acceptable product/security boundary.

options.title: Narrow safe commands first
options.body: Approve only explicit Android device-control commands that have Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused tests; defer ADB and arbitrary Kotlin execution.

options.title: Route execution through node-host/plugin APIs
options.body: Keep high-power ADB and dynamic execution out of the Android app and require a node-hosted plugin/tool path with existing exec approvals and policy controls.

options.title: Defer phone execution work
options.body: Leave this umbrella open for discussion but do not accept more Android control or execution surface until a maintainer-owned security design exists.

recommendation.title: Narrow safe commands first
recommendation.body: Approve only explicit Android device-control commands that have Android permission UX, gateway allowlist policy, and focused tests; defer ADB and arbitrary Kotlin execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and landed the related Android node work and already commented on the session product direction.
